name: Citizenship by Marriage (Foreign Wife of Guatemalan Husband)

requirement_groups.name: Nationality option exercised during marriage proceedings

requirements.blocker_text: Ley de Nacionalidad (Decreto 1613), Article 43: a foreign woman who marries a Guatemalan man may opt for Guatemalan nationality during the marriage proceedings themselves, when those proceedings take place in Guatemala. Remaining formalities are completed at the Ministry of Foreign Relations. Article 42 requires proof of marriage validity and that the marriage is still subsisting when more than one year has elapsed since the ceremony before the option is finalized.
requirements.fix_path: Marry a Guatemalan citizen with the ceremony conducted in Guatemala, exercise the nationality option during the marriage proceedings, and complete formalities at the Ministry of Foreign Relations.

evidence_required.document: Proof of marriage validity / subsistence (if >1 year since ceremony)

sources.title: UNHCR (ACNUR) -- hosted primary legal text of Guatemala's Ley de Nacionalidad, Decreto 1613 (29 October 1966) and reforms, Articles 42-45 (marriage-based nationality) and Article 5 (dual nationality, as modified by Decreto 86-1996)

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Guatemala). STATUS: DRAFT -- the only source located hosting the actual legal text is UNHCR/ACNUR (tier 2, not a Guatemalan government domain directly); Guatemala's own gob.gt hosting of this specific law was not located in this build. STARK, EXPLICITLY DISCLOSED GENDER ASYMMETRY: Article 43 grants the nationality-option ONLY to a foreign WOMAN marrying a Guatemalan MAN -- no equivalent provision for a foreign man marrying a Guatemalan woman was found anywhere in this 1966 law (as amended). This mirrors the same one-directional pattern found in this dataset's Syria marriage-citizenship file. Article 45 separately confirms Guatemalan women who marry a foreigner keep their own nationality unless they explicitly adopt the husband's -- so Guatemala does not strip nationality from its own women on marriage (a real protection), but does not extend the reciprocal acquisition right to foreign men. dual_citizenship_allowed left null for this specific route: Article 5 (as amended 1996) addresses dual nationality generally for Guatemalans, but the source did not confirm whether a foreign wife acquiring nationality under Article 43 must renounce her original citizenship -- disclosed as unconfirmed rather than assumed either way. citizenship_after_months set 0 to reflect that the option can be exercised at the time of the marriage proceedings themselves when conducted in Guatemala, though Article 42's >1-year documentation requirement can add practical delay for marriages formalized differently -- this nuance is disclosed rather than smoothed over. This is the current-law finding this build could confirm; an earlier, much older 1868 immigration-law marriage-naturalization privilege referenced in a secondary academic source was NOT used here since Decreto 1613 (1966, as amended) is the current governing law.
